'''Mie celor''' ({{lit|blanched noodle}} in [[Indonesian language|Indonesian]]) is a [[Southeast Asia]]n [[noodle soup]] dish served in a [[coconut milk]] and [[Shrimp and prawn as food|shrimp]]-based broth, specialty of [[Palembang]] city, [[South Sumatra]], [[Indonesia]].<ref>{{cite book | last=Kraig | first=B. | last2=Sen | first2=C.T. | title=Street Food Around the World: An Encyclopedia of Food and Culture | publisher=ABC-CLIO | year=2013 | isbn=978-1-59884-955-4 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=9XCjAQAAQBAJ&pg=PA184 | access-date=May 1, 2017 | page=184}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title=Mie Celor Palembang | date=November 18, 2013 | url=http://ridhaskitchen.com/2013/11/18/mie-celor-palembang/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131126094934/http://ridhaskitchen.com/2013/11/18/mie-celor-palembang/ | url-status=usurped | archive-date=November 26, 2013 | publisher=Ridha's Kitchen | access-date=May 20, 2014 }}</ref>

Next to [[pempek]], mie celor is widely associated with Palembang city, despite this noodles might be sold in other cities in Sumatra. Certain restaurants in Palembang specialised on serving and selling this flavourful shrimp noodles with their specific recipe inherited for generations.<ref name ="Kompas-mie celor">{{Cite web|author=Boy|date=2008-02-05|title=Mie Celor 26 Ilir, Santapan Pulang Kampung|url=https://megapolitan.kompas.com/read/2008/02/05/15242777/mie.celor.26.ilir.santapan.pulang.kampung|access-date=2021-03-11|website=KOMPAS.com|language=id}}</ref>
